summary.title: Home Assistant confined — Figure 8.2 of the submission
summary.description: Figure 8.2 of the capstone submission: the confined design, drawn on the same canvas as Figure 8.1 so the delta is legible. VISUALISATION ONLY — no threats are enumerated here; they are derived by STRIDE per boundary within an ISO 31000 process, and Threat Dragon's own threat generator was not used. Five boundaries read EXISTS or UNCHANGED; TB2 reads NARROWED (finding F45) and carries residual risk R3. Generated by figures/fig_8_2_confined.py; edit that script rather than this file.

text.text:
Compare with Figure 8.1. Five flows drawn there are absent here — F4b (the shared hass.data dict), F5 (reads any integration's stored credentials), F6 (arbitrary file read via hass.config.path),
F8 (direct object access between integrations) and F9 (local network access). None of the five is refused by a check. The config entry store and secrets.yaml are not in the sandbox's
mount namespace, the two integrations are separate processes, and non-public destinations are denied by default, so there is no request to make.

data.name:
Compare with Figure 8.1. Five flows drawn there are absent here — F4b (the shared hass.data dict), F5 (reads any integration's stored credentials), F6 (arbitrary file read via hass.config.path),
F8 (direct object access between integrations) and F9 (local network access). None of the five is refused by a check. The config entry store and secrets.yaml are not in the sandbox's
mount namespace, the two integrations are separate processes, and non-public destinations are denied by default, so there is no request to make.

text.text:
TB5 and TB6 are crossed by no flow at all, and that is deliberate rather than an omission: in Figure 8.1 those same two locations carried F5, F6, F8, F4b and F9. A boundary nothing crosses is the
strongest form this design produces, because nothing has to decide correctly for it to hold.

text.text:
TB2 is narrowed, not closed. The mediator connects as an ordinary Home Assistant user that the bridge designates, so it can no longer create users, change the configuration or install integrations,
but it can still operate every device, because the platform's per-domain policy cannot be configured through a supported interface. That is residual risk R3, High, narrowed. Flow A is new: no grant reaches
a sandbox until a person has approved exactly what was shown (F57).
